analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, with no patch hunks and no code. No executable security behavior changes in them, and I found no concrete regression visible in these lines.

The changelog describes security-relevant source changes that this batch does not include. Later passes should check the corresponding code against the threat model:
- Cache routing persistence (CHANGELOG.md ~L354-358): cache holders and observed demand are written to the DB across restarts. Relevant to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache and timing oracle) and T-003. Check that no prompt text or raw chain hashes are persisted, and that restored holders bind only to live provider capabilities.
- SSD cache TTL doubled from 15 to 30 minutes (L477) and write budget raised from 150 to 750 GB/day (L395). Relevant to T-041 and T-016. The changelog says SEC-035 was re-accepted in the threat model, which cannot be confirmed from the supplied canonical context.
- Cached-prompt pricing (L427-435): billing depends on provider-reported `cached_tokens`. Check that malformed reports bill at the full input price and that the cache-read discount cannot be abused. This is a billing/ledger concern (A-009, ADV-001).
- Public model-demand stats (L521-530): k-anonymity thresholds of 20 requests and 3 accounts, a 1-hour publication delay, and 31-day aggregates. Check against T-058/T-059 (identity linkage and erasure).
- Coordinator legacy-compat cleanup (L446-458):
  - Removed the unauthenticated earnings lookup (T-031).
  - Attestation challenges now fail closed on missing status_signature or secure_boot_enabled (TB-009).
  - App Attest serves protocol 3 only (TB-011, T-052..T-058).
  - `EIGENINFERENCE_MIN_PROVIDER_VERSION` now also excludes providers that report no version. The live env value needs a manual raise before deploy.
- App Attest key rotation (L542-547): bounded rotation admission, serialized with machine merges; relevant to T-055.
- Autopilot (L240-250): the default is observation only. Check that live control is session-bound and cannot be abused by a malicious provider.
- Advisory threat-model review workflow (L388-391): executes only the trusted base revision.

No unchanged callers were examined; code for these items is outside this batch.
